input.title: Vetra remote drives enable team collaboration by syncing specifications across developers

input.description: Teams share a remote Vetra drive via --remote-drive flag. Preview drives let you test locally before syncing to the team.

input.content:
Vetra supports collaborative development through remote drives:

- **Without `--remote-drive`**: Creates a local drive in browser local storage (solo development)
- **With `--remote-drive <url>`**: Connects to a shared remote drive

Key workflows:
- **Project Owner**: `ph init --remote-drive <url>` -> Create GitHub repo -> Push -> `ph vetra --watch`
- **Collaborator**: `ph checkout --remote-drive <url>` -> `ph vetra --watch`

The **preview drive** (created with `--watch` mode) provides a safe testing environment:
- The main "Vetra" drive syncs with the remote and contains stable configuration
- The "Vetra Preview" drive is local-only for testing document models and editors before syncing

Remote drive configuration is stored in `powerhouse.config.json`:
```json
"vetra": {
  "driveId": "bai-specifications",
  "driveUrl": "https://switchboard.staging.vetra.io/d/bai-specifications"
}
```

Vetra supports collaborative development through remote drives:

- **Without `--remote-drive`**: `ph vetra` boots a local Vetra Switchboard and creates the drive there (solo development)
- **With `--remote-drive <url>`**: Connects to a shared remote drive, skipping local switchboard initialization

Key workflows:
- **Project Owner**: `ph init --remote-drive <url>` -> Create GitHub repo -> Push -> `ph vetra --watch`
- **Collaborator**: `git clone <repo>` -> `pnpm install` -> `ph vetra --watch`

⚠️ **The collaborator step used to be `ph checkout --remote-drive <url>`, and that command no longer exists as far as the CLI is concerned.** It survives only as `clis/ph-cmd/legacy/commands/checkout.ts`, registered in neither `phCliCommandNames` (`packages/shared/clis/command-names.ts`) nor the `ph` entrypoint's cmd-ts subcommand tree (`clis/ph-cmd/src/commands/ph.ts` → `init`, `use`, `update`, `setup-globals`, `use-local` + help commands). The `legacy/` directory is excluded from tsconfig and never built or published; the file would not even compile, since it imports a `../utils/package-manager.js` that does not exist. The academy still teaches it in five places across two pages, and `COMMANDS-LEGACY.md` documents it as well — all stale. There is no replacement command: `ph init --remote-drive` is for *creating* a project bound to a drive, so joining an existing one is the manual clone-and-install shown above.

The clone works as a substitute for one specific reason: the repo's committed `powerhouse.config.json` already carries the `vetra` block, and `ph vetra`'s `--remote-drive` option has a `defaultValue` that reads `getConfig().vetra?.driveUrl`. So a fresh clone picks up the team's drive with no flags. If the block is missing, hand-edit it in or pass `ph vetra --remote-drive <url>` every time — nothing in the CLI can write that key after `ph init` (its only two writers are codegen scaffold paths, and `getConfig` is read-only). Note also that only `driveUrl` is ever read back; `driveId` is written and then ignored.

Be aware of a live trap on the owner's side too: if you point `ph init --remote-drive` at a drive that has already been configured with a GitHub URL, `clis/ph-cli/src/utils/validate-remote-drive.ts` prints an error telling you to "use the checkout command instead" — the dead command — and because `clis/ph-cli/src/services/init.ts` ignores that validation failure, it then reports success and scaffolds a new project regardless.

The **preview drive** (created with `--watch` / `-w` mode) provides a safe testing environment:
- The main "Vetra" drive syncs with the remote and contains stable configuration
- The "Vetra Preview" drive is local-only for testing document models and editors before syncing

Remote drive configuration is stored in `powerhouse.config.json`:
```json
"vetra": {
  "driveId": "bai-specifications",
  "driveUrl": "https://switchboard.staging.vetra.io/d/bai-specifications"
}
```

Its type is `vetra?: { driveId: string; driveUrl: string }` (`packages/shared/clis/types.ts`), and the JSON schema marks both fields required with `additionalProperties: false`.

_Source-verified 2026-08-13 against Powerhouse source at v6.2.2-dev.45._

input.description: Teams share a remote Vetra drive via --remote-drive. Collaborators clone and run ph vetra, which reads the config; ph checkout is legacy. Preview drives test locally first.
